events.label: The Treta Yuga
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: The second age in the Puranic tradition. Dharma is described as three parts of four. It is also the age of the Ramayana tradition, whose figures never appear on screen.

events.label: The Southern Road at Dusk
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: A rough forest road at dusk, with monkeys rattling the branches. You carry healing herbs and keep them dry across a stream. The road is a story setting, not a mapped place.

events.label: The Ramayana Tradition
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: A long-loved epic, told in many languages and versions. The game only refers to it and shows none of its people. Please read it in its own retellings.

events.label: The Camp of Stone and Rope
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: Workers haul stone and rope by the sea in the tradition of the great causeway. You bring them water and cloth. Only the labour is shown, never any figure from the story.

events.label: The Shoals Called Rama Setu
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: A chain of shoals between India and Sri Lanka is known by this name and as Adam's Bridge. It is sacred to many people. The game gives no account of how it formed.

events.label: Household and Altar Fire
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: Keeping a hearth fire is an old practice in many households and rites. Later Vedic fire altars are dated by scholars to different centuries. The dates were not checked here.

events.label: The Hall of Small Fires
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: One ember in a clay pot must last until dawn in a windy hall. Keep it small, keep it fed, and keep the village asleep.

events.label: Herbal Medicine and Ayurveda
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: Ayurveda is a living medical tradition with old texts such as the Charaka and Sushruta compilations. Their dates are debated and were not checked here. The game uses it only as inspiration.

events.label: The Herb Path
events.source: docs/timeline-levels.md (studio draft, not yet checked against a primary source)
events.intro: At night in the forest a child is lost, and a bell is the only guide. Stay calm so that startled animals pass by. This is the keystone of the Treta ring.
